passage:
A volunteer group made a map of free indoor places people could use during extreme heat: libraries, malls, temples, community centers, and subway stations.
They included opening hours, water availability, and wheelchair access.
The map helped delivery workers, older people, and families without air conditioning.
A student volunteer realized that information can be life-saving during heat waves. A cool room is useful only if people know where it is and feel welcome there.
The map was simple, but it treated heat as a public problem, not only a private discomfort.
Climate adaptation often begins with knowing who needs help and where help exists.
